title: Carolers
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small-town 911 dispatch center at night and snowy suburban streets on Christmas Eve, dim console glow, cold green and deep red tones, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 2. A dozen sets of footprints circled the house. Nobody was there. 🎶

Original fiction. Part 3 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: on Christmas Eve, an old man called 911 from a house with no phone line and said: they're singing outside again.
scenes.image: a dispatcher at a glowing console late at night, snow at the window behind her

scenes.narration: Officer Dale Brooks reached Larkspur Road at ten past midnight. Snow up to his shins. No streetlights.
scenes.image: a police officer with a flashlight stepping out of a patrol car into deep snow on a dark road

scenes.narration: Number eighteen was dark. Windows boarded. A wreath on the door, brown and brittle, years old.
scenes.image: old boarded-up two-story house in snow with a brittle brown wreath on the door

scenes.narration: He radioed in. Nobody home, June. Nobody's lived here in a long time.
scenes.image: close-up of a police radio clipped to a snowy uniform shoulder

scenes.narration: Then his voice changed. June. There are footprints.
scenes.image: flashlight beam sweeping across trampled snow beside a dark house

scenes.narration: Fresh ones. A dozen sets. Not wandering. Single file, in a perfect circle around the house, packed hard into the snow. Around and around and around.
scenes.image: aerial view of a lone snowy house surrounded by a perfect packed ring of footprints

scenes.narration: A dozen people walked around that house a hundred times. Not one of them walked away.
scenes.image: a ring of footprints in snow with no trail leading out of it, moonlight

scenes.narration: June asked if he saw anyone. He said no. Then he went quiet for a long time. Too long. She asked if he was okay.
scenes.image: dispatcher leaning toward her console, hand pressed to her headset

scenes.narration: He said: June, I can hear singing. It's coming from inside. Every window's boarded. And somebody just lit a candle.
scenes.image: a single candle flame glowing through the gap in a boarded window of a dark house in snow

scenes.narration: Then Dale stopped talking. And over his open radio, a dozen voices began the second verse.
scenes.image: an empty patrol car with its door open and lights glowing on a snowy road at night
